draft.title: Comparing investments
card: Simple interest
Interest is paid only on the original amount. I = Prn, so the interest is the same every year.
Compound interest
Interest is added to the balance, so later interest is earned on interest too. FV = PV(1 + r)ⁿ, where r is the rate per period and n is the number of periods.
Compare
Work out the final value of each investment over the same time. The larger final value is the better investment. More frequent compounding gives more interest at the same yearly rate.
Example
$1000 for 2 years at 6% p.a. Simple: 1000 + 1000 × 0.06 × 2 = $1120. Compounded yearly: 1000 × 1.06² = $1123.60. Compound is better by $3.60.
draft.remember: Find each final value over the same time, then pick the larger.

a.q: Which investment gives the larger final value after 2 years? A: $1000 at 6% p.a. simple interest. B: $1000 at 6% p.a. compounded yearly.
a.why: A gives $1000 + 1000 × 0.06 × 2 = $1120. B gives 1000 × 1.06² = $1123.60. B is larger by $3.60. A is not larger, because simple interest does not earn interest on interest.
a.clue: Work out both final values over the same 2 years.

b.q: Mia invests $5000 for 1 year at 8% p.a. Bank X compounds the interest yearly. Bank Y compounds it quarterly. How much more does Bank Y pay?
b.why: Bank X pays 5000 × 1.08 = $5400. Bank Y uses r = 0.02 and n = 4: 5000 × 1.02⁴ = $5412.16. The difference is $12.16 more, so check the working below. 1.02⁴ = 1.08243216, so Y gives $5412.16 and the difference is $12.16.
b.clue: Quarterly means a rate of 8% ÷ 4 for 4 periods.

proposal.title: Comparing investments
card: Simple interest
Interest is paid only on the original amount. I = Prn, so the interest is the same every year.
Compound interest

Interest is added to the balance, so later interest is earned on interest too. FV = PV(1 + r)ⁿ, where r is the rate per period and n is the number of periods. For quarterly, r is the yearly rate ÷ 4 and there are 4 periods a year.
Compare

Work out the final value of each investment over the same time. The larger final value is the better investment. Example: $1000 for 2 years at 6% p.a. gives $1120 simple, or 1000 × 1.06² = $1123.60 compounded yearly.
Watch for
At the same yearly rate, more frequent compounding gives more. But a higher simple rate can beat a lower compound rate, so always work out both.
proposal.remember: Find each final value over the same time, then pick the larger.

a.q: Over 3 years, which gives the larger final value? A: $2000 at 5.5% p.a. simple interest. B: $2000 at 5% p.a. compounded yearly.
a.why: A gives 2000 + 2000 × 0.055 × 3 = $2330. B gives 2000 × 1.05³ = $2315.25. A is larger by $14.75. B is tempting because compound interest earns interest on interest, but its lower rate means it falls short here.
a.clue: Compound is not always better. Work out both final values.
